statement: Declarative rules over typed facts: which statement of a document covers which value (scope), which kind a value is and how that is justified, and when two values compare. Negation reads the record, never the world: 'not stated' means the record does not state it. Every predicate has one meaning in every program; a predicate derived by one program may be an input of another. kr.2 (WD, 2026-10-18) adds program record: which values of one record (a table row, a sentence) are the conditions of its other values (principle P1, from the KV validation). kr.3 (R1, 2026-10-18): a difference of conditions is concluded only when it is documented or follows from definitions (two ranks of one ordinal series, highest vs lowest, two numbers in one unit); otherwise two stated values are 'not shown equal'. The verdict is unchanged (not comparable); the reason no longer claims more than the record shows. rules.v2.json is kept for reproduction.

vocabulary.name: value
vocabulary.meaning: O is a printed value being typed or compared.

vocabulary.name: candidate_kind
vocabulary.meaning: K is a quantity kind O can still be, after its unit and its own words.

vocabulary.name: local_kind
vocabulary.meaning: O's own unit and words leave exactly one kind, K.

vocabulary.name: unit_only_kind
vocabulary.meaning: O's unit can express only kind K.

vocabulary.name: unit_reference_kind
vocabulary.meaning: O's unit names a reference (re 1 pW) that only kind K has.

vocabulary.name: local_evidence
vocabulary.meaning: Word X, which the knowledge types as justification T for kind K, occurs in O's labels (F=labels) or its context (F=context).

vocabulary.name: metric_named
vocabulary.meaning: O's labels (F=labels) or context (F=context) name metric M, whose kind is K.

vocabulary.name: evidence_class
vocabulary.meaning: The table reader classed O as evidence class C (publisher_measured, manufacturer_declared, unknown, ...).

vocabulary.name: value_product
vocabulary.meaning: O is attributed to the product named P.

vocabulary.name: block_evidence
vocabulary.meaning: Document block B contains word X, which the knowledge types as justification T for kind K.

vocabulary.name: block_measurand
vocabulary.meaning: Block B names the measurand family of kind K (noise, sound, ...).

vocabulary.name: block_restates
vocabulary.meaning: Block B prints O's value again (same number, same kind of unit).

vocabulary.name: block_in_table
vocabulary.meaning: Block B is a cell (an info note, a footnote row) of the table O is printed in.

vocabulary.name: block_names_product
vocabulary.meaning: Block B names product P by its full name.

vocabulary.name: next_block
vocabulary.meaning: B2 is the next text block after B1 in the same section.

vocabulary.name: covers_class
vocabulary.meaning: The knowledge says a document-wide statement of justification T for kind K covers values of evidence class C.

vocabulary.name: justification_rank
vocabulary.meaning: Strength N of justification T found at F (higher wins; at equal type the value's own words beat the document).

vocabulary.name: method_block
vocabulary.meaning: S states how values were obtained or under which scheme: it names an instrument, a scheme or a quantity.

vocabulary.name: statement_part
vocabulary.meaning: Block B is part of the statement S (S itself and the two blocks that follow it in its section).

vocabulary.name: statement_about
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S is about the measurand family of kind K.

vocabulary.name: statement_says
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S contains word X of justification T for kind K.

vocabulary.name: statement_restates
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S prints O's value again.

vocabulary.name: statement_names_product
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S names product P.

vocabulary.name: statement_covers
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S applies to value O before its product scope is checked.

vocabulary.name: other_product_statement
vocabulary.meaning: S names products but not the product of O, so it is not about O.

vocabulary.name: in_scope
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S applies to value O.

vocabulary.name: supports
vocabulary.meaning: Statement S supports kind K for O with justification T.

vocabulary.name: names_kind_elsewhere
vocabulary.meaning: The document names kind K explicitly in a statement that does not restate O (a possible defeater).

vocabulary.name: supported
vocabulary.meaning: Some in-scope statement supports kind K for O.

vocabulary.name: document_conflict
vocabulary.meaning: The document's statements support or name more than one kind for O.

vocabulary.name: open_kind
vocabulary.meaning: O's own unit and words leave more than one kind.

vocabulary.name: kind_by_document
vocabulary.meaning: The document settles O's kind as K (defeasibly, only where O's own words leave it open).

vocabulary.name: kind_of
vocabulary.meaning: O's kind is established as K.

vocabulary.name: justification_candidate0
vocabulary.meaning: Evidence X at F justifies O's established kind with type T.

vocabulary.name: justified0
vocabulary.meaning: Some typed evidence justifies O's established kind.

vocabulary.name: justification_candidate
vocabulary.meaning: A justification of O's kind (typed evidence, or the discriminating words when no typed evidence exists).

vocabulary.name: justification_score
vocabulary.meaning: A justification candidate with its strength.

vocabulary.name: outranked
vocabulary.meaning: A stronger justification than strength N exists for O.

vocabulary.name: best_justification
vocabulary.meaning: The strongest justification of O's kind.

vocabulary.name: has_kind
vocabulary.meaning: O's kind is established.

vocabulary.name: kind_unjustified
vocabulary.meaning: Nothing establishes O's kind: its justification is insufficient.

vocabulary.name: context_statement
vocabulary.meaning: S is a text near the table that the reader offers as context for its values: F=frame (caption, heading: it frames every value of the table) or F=nearby (a paragraph before or beside the table).

vocabulary.name: context_other_product
vocabulary.meaning: Context S names products, but not the product of O.

vocabulary.name: context_applies
vocabulary.meaning: Context S applies to value O: its metric names, condition cues and method names may be read for O.

vocabulary.name: metric_of
vocabulary.meaning: Value V is established as metric M.

vocabulary.name: metric_label
vocabulary.meaning: L is the readable name of metric M.

vocabulary.name: not_equivalent
vocabulary.meaning: The knowledge says metrics M1 and M2 are not equivalent.

vocabulary.name: level_value
vocabulary.meaning: V is a level (dB-type) value.

vocabulary.name: weighting
vocabulary.meaning: V's frequency weighting is W (A, C, Z or unspecified).

vocabulary.name: conventional_basis
vocabulary.meaning: V's unit has a conventional reporting basis (per 100 cycles, per year).

vocabulary.name: unit_expression
vocabulary.meaning: V's unit expression is E.

vocabulary.name: required_condition
vocabulary.meaning: The knowledge requires condition axis X to compare V.

vocabulary.name: stated_condition
vocabulary.meaning: The record states condition X = W for V.

vocabulary.name: presented_test
vocabulary.meaning: V is printed in the test C its source presents (same table, same labels apart from the product).

vocabulary.name: finding_stage_final
vocabulary.meaning: The last stage of the comparability check is reached when nothing earlier is found.

vocabulary.name: shared_kind
vocabulary.meaning: a and b can be the same kind.

vocabulary.name: same_kind
vocabulary.meaning: a and b are established as the same kind.

vocabulary.name: has_metric
vocabulary.meaning: V is established as some metric.

vocabulary.name: some_level
vocabulary.meaning: a or b is a level.

vocabulary.name: weighting_differs
vocabulary.meaning: a and b have different weightings.

vocabulary.name: weighting_unspecified
vocabulary.meaning: a or b has an unspecified weighting.

vocabulary.name: some_conventional
vocabulary.meaning: a or b has a conventional reporting basis.

vocabulary.name: relevant_condition
vocabulary.meaning: Condition X matters for comparing a and b: required for either, or stated for either.

vocabulary.name: stated_both
vocabulary.meaning: The record states X for both a and b.

vocabulary.name: common_value
vocabulary.meaning: a and b share a stated value of X.

vocabulary.name: unestablished
vocabulary.meaning: X is relevant but not stated for both.

vocabulary.name: some_unestablished
vocabulary.meaning: Some relevant condition is not stated for both.

vocabulary.name: one_presented_test
vocabulary.meaning: a and b are printed in one test C their source presents, and their kind is justified.

vocabulary.name: finding
vocabulary.meaning: At stage S of the comparability check, finding R leads to verdict V.

vocabulary.name: earlier_finding
vocabulary.meaning: A finding at a stage before S exists.

vocabulary.name: verdict
vocabulary.meaning: The comparability verdict V, for reason R.

vocabulary.name: rec_value
vocabulary.meaning: V is a printed value of record R (one table row with a record axis, one sentence, one key-value pair).

vocabulary.name: rec_kind
vocabulary.meaning: V is established as a quantity of kind K.

vocabulary.name: rec_metric
vocabulary.meaning: V is named as metric M by its own words.

vocabulary.name: rec_point
vocabulary.meaning: V is a single value, not a range or a bound (a test condition is a set point; an operating range is a specification).

vocabulary.name: metric_requires
vocabulary.meaning: The knowledge says metric M is comparable only with condition axis A stated.

vocabulary.name: axis_value_kind
vocabulary.meaning: Condition axis A takes values that are quantities of kind K.

vocabulary.name: rec_has_metric
vocabulary.meaning: V names a metric of its own.

vocabulary.name: rec_requires
vocabulary.meaning: A value of record R needs condition axis A.

vocabulary.name: rec_condition_value
vocabulary.meaning: V is the value of condition A for the results of record R.

vocabulary.name: rec_is_condition
vocabulary.meaning: V is a condition of its record, not a result.

vocabulary.name: rec_condition
vocabulary.meaning: Result W of a record was obtained under condition A, whose value is V.

vocabulary.name: condition_rank
vocabulary.meaning: V's condition X is rank N of the ordinal series S (speed 3: series speed, rank 3).

vocabulary.name: condition_number
vocabulary.meaning: V's condition X is the number N in unit U.

vocabulary.name: disjoint_values
vocabulary.meaning: By definition, values W1 and W2 of axis X are different states (the highest and the lowest setting).

vocabulary.name: documented_distinct
vocabulary.meaning: The pair's values of condition X are different states, by the record or by definition.

vocabulary.name: named_value
vocabulary.meaning: W is a value the knowledge names for axis X (a closed list: pollutants, floor types, gamuts, methods).

vocabulary.name: operating_axis
vocabulary.meaning: Axis X is an operating setting (fan setting, programme, signal mode): its names can refer to one state.

programs.statement: Which statements of a document apply to a value, what kind the value is, and how that is justified.

rules.statement: A block naming an instrument, a declared scheme or a quantity states how values were obtained.
A method block is part of its own statement.
The block after a method sentence (its results) belongs to the statement.
So does the block after that, within the same section.
A statement is about the measurand its parts name.
An instrument the knowledge ties to a kind (a sound level meter) makes the statement about that kind's measurand.
Naming the quantity itself makes the statement about it. A declared scheme (an energy label) also covers other quantities, so it still needs the measurand named.
A statement says what its parts say.
A statement restates a value one of its parts prints again.
A statement names the products its parts name.
A statement that prints the value again speaks about that value.
A method note inside a table speaks about that table's values, whatever class its heading suggests.
A document-wide statement covers the evidence classes the knowledge names for it (an instrument covers the publisher's readings, a label scheme covers declarations).
A statement that names products, but not the product of a value, is not about that value.
rules.source: KR (owner review: a methodology does not necessarily cover every observation)

rules.statement: A statement applies to a value it covers, unless it is about other products.

rules.rule: supports(O,K,T,S) :- candidate_kind(O,K), in_scope(S,O), statement_about(S,K), statement_says(S,K,T,_), T != contextual, T != explicit.
rules.statement: An applicable statement about the measurand supports the kind its instrument or scheme establishes.

rules.rule: supports(O,K,explicit,S) :- candidate_kind(O,K), statement_restates(S,O), not other_product_statement(S,O), statement_about(S,K), statement_says(S,K,explicit,_).
rules.statement: A statement that prints the value again and names its quantity supports that quantity explicitly.

rules.rule: names_kind_elsewhere(O,K) :- candidate_kind(O,K), statement_about(S,K), statement_says(S,K,explicit,_), not statement_restates(S,O).
rules.statement: A quantity the document names elsewhere is a possible alternative for the value.
A kind is supported when some applicable statement supports it.
Statements supporting two kinds conflict.
A supported kind conflicts with another kind the document names.
Naming two kinds is a conflict.
A value whose own words leave two kinds is open.
The document settles an open value's kind when its applicable statements agree (defeasible: the value's own words come first, a conflict withdraws it).
The value's own unit and words settle its kind.
Otherwise the document may settle it.
An applicable statement supporting the established kind justifies it.
A unit that expresses one kind justifies it.
A unit reference (re 1 pW) names the kind explicitly.
Typed words of the value's labels or context justify the kind with their type, when they are what settled it (a kind the document settled is justified by the document).
A metric the labels name states the kind explicitly.
A metric named only in the context is a contextual justification.
The kind has typed justification.
Typed justifications are candidates.
Without typed justification, the discriminating words are a contextual justification.
Each justification has a strength.
A weaker justification is outranked.
The reported justification is the strongest.
The kind is established.
A value whose kind nothing establishes has insufficient justification; it stays ambiguous.

programs.statement: Whether two values a and b compare, and why: the first stage with a finding decides.

rules.statement: a and b can be the same kind.
a and b are established as the same kind.
V is established as a metric.
A level is involved.
The weightings differ.
A weighting is unspecified.
A conventional reporting basis is involved.
A condition the knowledge requires for either value matters.
A condition stated for either value matters.
The record states the condition for both.
Both share a stated value.
A relevant condition the record does not state for both is unestablished (not absent).
rules.source: GK; owner review: not documented is not scientifically absent

rules.statement: Some condition is unestablished.

rules.rule: one_presented_test(C) :- presented_test(a,C), presented_test(b,C), value_product(a,P), value_product(b,Q), P != Q, not kind_unjustified(a), not kind_unjustified(b).
rules.statement: a and b are printed in one test their source presents, for different products. Two values of one product under the same labels are one test only when their records state the same conditions (P1: then the stated conditions decide, stage 7, before this one); with nothing stated, something the record does not show tells them apart (KV P2, now a consequence of P1).
by definition different settings (highest vs lowest).
two ranks of one ordinal series are different settings.
two different numbers in one unit are different conditions.

rules.rule: documented_distinct(X) :- stated_condition(a,X,W1), stated_condition(b,X,W2), W1 != W2, named_value(X,W1), named_value(X,W2), not operating_axis(X).
rules.statement: two different named values of a closed list that is not an operating setting (dust vs smoke; two named methods) are different conditions by definition.
Values that cannot be the same quantity do not compare.
Which quantity is meant must be established on both sides.
rules.explain: which quantity is meant is not established ({@candidate_kind(a,*)} vs {@candidate_kind(b,*)})

rules.rule: finding(3,not_comparable,different_metrics) :- metric_of(a,M1), metric_of(b,M2), M1 != M2, not not_equivalent(M1,M2).
rules.statement: Different metrics do not compare.
Metrics the knowledge declares not equivalent do not compare.
rules.explain: different metrics: {M1} vs {M2} (the knowledge says they are not equivalent)

rules.statement: A metric established on one side only leaves the comparison undetermined.
rules.explain: only one side is established as {@metric_label(*)}; the other is a {@kind_of(b,*)} of unstated definition

rules.statement: A metric established on one side only leaves the comparison undetermined.
rules.explain: only one side is established as {@metric_label(*)}; the other is a {@kind_of(a,*)} of unstated definition

rules.statement: An unspecified weighting leaves a level comparison undetermined.
rules.explain: frequency weighting not established on both sides ({@weighting(a,*)} vs {@weighting(b,*)})

rules.statement: Levels of different weightings do not compare.

rules.rule: finding(6,not_comparable,different_bases) :- some_conventional, unit_expression(a,E1), unit_expression(b,E2), E1 != E2.
rules.statement: A conventional reporting basis is not converted.
rules.explain: different reporting bases ({E1} vs {E2}); a conventional basis is not converted

rules.statement: the two values were obtained under conditions the record or the definitions show to be different.
rules.source: WD; kr.3 (R1) bounded to documented differences

rules.rule: finding(7,not_comparable,conditions_not_shown_equal) :- relevant_condition(X), stated_both(X), not common_value(X), not documented_distinct(X).
rules.statement: the two values state different names for a condition, and nothing shows that they are the same state or different states (sleep vs speed 1): not comparable, relation unknown.
rules.explain: {X} named differently ({@stated_condition(a,X,*)} vs {@stated_condition(b,X,*)}); not shown to be the same state or different states

rules.statement: Values of one test their source presents share the conditions it leaves unstated: they compare with each other, never with other sources or other tests.
rules.explain: same quantity in one test the source presents; not established: {@unestablished(*)}, so not comparable with other sources or other tests of this source

rules.statement: Unestablished conditions leave the comparison open.
rules.explain: same quantity; not established on both sides: {@unestablished(*)}

rules.statement: Otherwise the values compare.
A finding at an earlier stage takes precedence.
The verdict is the earliest finding.

programs.statement: Which texts near a table apply to a value: the frame always, a nearby paragraph unless it is about other products.

rules.statement: The table's caption and heading frame every value of the table.

rules.rule: context_other_product(S,O) :- context_statement(S,nearby), block_names_product(S,_), value_product(O,Q), not block_names_product(S,Q).
rules.statement: A nearby paragraph that names products, but not the value's product, is not about that value.
rules.source: KR2 (owner review: a methodology does not necessarily cover every observation)

rules.statement: Otherwise a nearby paragraph applies to the table's values (when the value's product is not established, nothing in the record says the paragraph is about another product).

programs.statement: P1: conditions belong to the test record, not to the metric. In one record, a single value with no metric of its own whose kind is what a condition axis takes, where a co-recorded result needs that axis, is a condition of the record; it applies to every result of the record, whatever its metric.

rules.statement: V names a metric of its own.
a result of the record names a metric that needs condition axis A.

rules.rule: rec_condition_value(V,A,R) :- rec_value(V,R), rec_point(V), rec_kind(V,K), axis_value_kind(A,K), rec_requires(R,A), not rec_has_metric(V).
rules.statement: a single value of the record, of a kind axis A takes, with no metric of its own, is the record's value of A.
V is a condition, not a result.

rules.rule: rec_condition(W,A,V) :- rec_condition_value(V,A,R), rec_value(W,R), W != V, not rec_is_condition(W), rec_kind(W,KW), not axis_value_kind(A,KW).
rules.statement: every result of the record was obtained under the record's conditions, whatever its metric (wattage at a rating point too). A value of a kind the axis itself takes (another temperature) is not measured under it.
